Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: A National e-Government Framework exists (contractor-developed since 2019) and digital transformation is mentioned in national economic conference papers (Sept 2023). No comprehensive dedicated interoperability strategy found. Data exchange is mentioned in broader digital economy aspirations but not a standalone strategy.
revision_notes: Original cited URLs checked: the mofp.gov.ss PDF returned a 403 error (dead/inaccessible) and mictps.gov.ss is only a general ministry site with no dedicated interoperability strategy document, so neither source substantively supports the score on its own. A focused search found stronger, more current evidence: the World Bank-financed Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP, 2023-2028, Grant E1780) includes Sub-component 2.2 'Data exchange, governance and protection', with a June 2024 Implementation Support Mission Aide-Memoire confirming a South Sudan Digital Development Road Map/Master Plan is being developed by a consulting firm and an EU-funded eGovt strategy draft has been handed to MICT&PS for review. These confirm data exchange/interoperability is addressed as a component within broader digital development and connectivity strategies, but no standalone, comprehensive government data exchange/interoperability strategy exists yet. Score of 2 (Mentioned in Broader DPI/Digital Strategy) is confirmed as accurate against the scale; sources and year updated to the more recent and authoritative World Bank mission documentation.
revised_comments: South Sudan does not yet have a standalone, comprehensive strategy or policy dedicated to government data exchange and interoperability. Data exchange is instead addressed as a sub-component of broader digital development initiatives: the World Bank-financed Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP, 2023-2028) includes a dedicated sub-component on data exchange, governance and protection (establishing internet exchange points and government data hosting/backup arrangements), and a South Sudan Digital Development Road Map/Master Plan and an EU-funded e-government strategy are both in development under the Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services (MICT&PS). As of mid-2024, these remain broader digital development and e-government frameworks that reference data exchange rather than a dedicated interoperability strategy in their own right.
